newsitem.title: USA: Boyds Wheels sees 1996 net below forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Boyds Wheels sees 1996 net below forecasts.

text.p: Boyds Wheels Inc said Tuesday it expects 1996 sales to rise $27.2 million from 1995, but net income will be lower than forecast, due in part to manufacturing inefficiency.
Sales for 1995 were $17.8 million, the company said.
Higher sales stemmed from aggressive marketing, growth of its two-piece cast wheel product line, and expansion into new products including one-piece cast wheels and motorcycle parts.
The company said it has completed a boost in its manufacturing capacity that will increase production.
Construction to add capacity caused "manufacturing inefficiencies" which hurt the company's bottom line, it said.
Also, higher than expected scrap rates and a less profitable foreign/domestic sales mix hurt profits, it said.
According to First Call, analysts' consensus earnings estimate for 1996 is $0.64 per share. In 1995 Boyds earned $0.48 per share.

"We believe our plan already under way to correct the manufacturing inefficiencies is sound and will be effective in our efforts to continue to grow the company," said Boyd Coddington, chief executive officer.
Boyds shares were off 2-1/2 at 11-3/4 at mid-morning.
The company said it will release 1996 financial results in March.
